frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully pass a joint resolution of disapproval to block a submitted Section 123 nuclear cooperation agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal presidential submissions of Section 123 agreements requiring congressional review; excludes informal notifications, non-nuclear trade agreements, and treaties requiring formal two-thirds Senate ratification.
provenance_note: claims 25 cases from only 3 named (8.3x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: Over 25 major peaceful nuclear cooperation agreements have entered into force without a successful congressional block.
known_gaps: Historical agreements prior to the 1980s often lacked the modern structured joint resolution mechanism, though none were successfully blocked via adverse legislation.
skeleton: Total formal Section 123 agreement submissions since statutory review mechanisms were established, where a joint resolution of disapproval was introduced.
multiplier: 0 successful blocks out of over 20 submitted agreements since the 1950s, with zero instances of a joint resolution passing both chambers and overriding a veto.
validity_reason: Statutory requirements for Section 123 agreements remain stable under the Atomic Energy Act unless major legislative reform occurs.
